title: Reconstructing a rational point from a tensor-compatible representation family
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], meaning every nonconstant polynomial in $K[T]$ has a root in $K$, and let $G$ be an affine $K$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A finite-dimensional rational representation $(V,r_V)$ means an algebraic-group module [def-wf-algebraic-representations]: $V$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space and $r_V:G\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ is a homomorphism of $K$-group schemes, where $\mathrm{GL}(V)(R)=\operatorname{Aut}_R(R\otimes_K V)$ for a commutative $K$-algebra $R$. The zero representation is permitted. A $G$-equivariant map $f:V\to W$ is $K$-linear and satisfies $(1_R\otimes f)r_V(x)=r_W(x)(1_R\otimes f)$ for every such $R$ and $x\in G(R)$. The tensor representation on $V\otimes_K W$ has action $r_{V\otimes W}(x)=r_V(x)\otimes_R r_W(x)$ under the canonical scalar-extension identification; the tensor product is universal for bilinear maps. The unit representation $\mathbf1$ is $K$ with trivial action. Suppose that for every finite-dimensional rational representation $(V,r_V)$ one is given an invertible $K$-linear map $\lambda_V:V\to V$. Assume $f\lambda_V=\lambda_Wf$ for every $G$-equivariant map $f:V\to W$, $\lambda_{V\otimes W}=\lambda_V\otimes\lambda_W$ for every pair of representations, and $\lambda_{\mathbf1}=\mathrm{id}_K$. Then there exists a unique $h\in G(K)$ such that $r_V(h)=\lambda_V$ for every finite-dimensional rational representation $V$. Here $G(R)$ denotes the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}R\to G$ over $K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. All spaces and algebras lie in a fixed universe, and the family is indexed in a containing universe.

source.place: Theorem 9.2 and conditions (a), (b), (c), printed pp.164--165, specialized to R=K and invertible maps; algebraic groups are affine by the convention at the end of Chapter 8, printed p.162.

proof.text: Put $A=K[G]$. Use [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] for its Hopf structure and [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] to express representations and equivariant maps as coactions and coaction-preserving linear maps. In particular, $A$ with coaction $\Delta$ is the right regular representation: the coaction identities are precisely coassociativity and the counit identity. Trivial and tensor representations have the coactions in the dictionary. We allow infinite-dimensional rational modules temporarily; only finite-dimensional ones carry the originally supplied maps.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, regular representation; Remark 4.1, printed p.84.

proof.text: For any rational module $M$ and $v\in M$, choose a finite-dimensional rational submodule $W$ containing $v$, using [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subrepresentation], and set $L_M(v)=\lambda_W(v)$, viewed in $M$. This does not depend on $W$: for two choices $W,Z$, choose finite spanning sets of each and apply the same cited node to their union to obtain a finite-dimensional rational submodule $T$ containing both. The inclusions are equivariant by [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], so naturality of the given family makes both values equal to $\lambda_T(v)$. Choosing one such $T$ for any two vectors also proves additivity and homogeneity. Thus $L_M$ is a linear map and equals the original $\lambda_M$ when $M$ is finite-dimensional.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed pp.164--165, extension to unions of finite-dimensional subrepresentations.

proof.text: The enlarged family is natural for every equivariant linear map $f:M\to N$. Choose a finite-dimensional submodule $W$ containing $v$ and a finite-dimensional submodule $Z$ of $N$ containing the images of a finite spanning set of $W$, using [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subrepresentation]. Then $f(W)\subseteq Z$. The restricted map $W\to Z$ commutes with coactions: its coaction equation becomes the original one after inclusion into $N\otimes A$, and that inclusion is injective. To check injectivity directly, choose a basis $(a_i)$ of $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free]. Expanding finite tensor sums in this basis and applying its coefficient maps [def-weil-pbc-free-module] shows that $\sum z_i\otimes a_i$ can vanish in $N\otimes A$ only when every $z_i=0$; these coefficient maps exist by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The dictionary [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] makes the restriction equivariant. Original naturality gives $fL_M(v)=L_Nf(v)$ for every $v$.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, condition (c) for the enlarged family.

proof.text: For arbitrary rational $M,N$, choose finite-dimensional rational submodules $W\subset M$, $Z\subset N$ containing $v,w$, respectively, by [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subrepresentation]. The tensor module $W\otimes Z$ is finite-dimensional: tensoring their finite spanning families gives a finite spanning family, by bilinearity and pure-tensor generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Its canonical map to $M\otimes N$ is equivariant by the tensor formula in [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. Step 3 for this map and original tensor compatibility give $L_{M\otimes N}(v\otimes w)=L_M(v)\otimes L_N(w)$. Since pure tensors span, $L_{M\otimes N}=L_M\otimes L_N$.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, condition (a) for the enlarged family.

proof.text: If $T$ is any vector space with trivial action and $t\in T$, the linear map $K\to T$, $a\mapsto at$, is equivariant by the trivial coaction formula [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. Apply step 3 and $\lambda_{\mathbf1}=1_K$ to $1$ to obtain $L_T(t)=t$. Thus $L_T=1_T$, including when $T$ is infinite-dimensional or zero.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, agreement on the underlying trivial vector space.

proof.text: Let $u=L_A$. Multiplication $m:A\otimes A\to A$ is equivariant for the diagonal tensor action: for $a,b\in A$, the equality $\Delta(ab)=\Delta(a)\Delta(b)$ says exactly $c_A m=(m\otimes1)c_{A\otimes A}$, by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] and the tensor formula [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. The unit $K\to A$ is equivariant since $\Delta(1)=1\otimes1$. Steps 3--5 therefore give $u(ab)=u(a)u(b)$ and $u(1)=1$. Linearity makes $u$ a $K$-algebra endomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, multiplication and unit on the regular representation.

proof.text:
Let $A_0$ denote the vector space $A$ with trivial action. The map $\Delta:A\to A_0\otimes A$ is equivariant: the target coaction is $1_A\otimes\Delta$, so the required equation is $(\Delta\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\Delta)\Delta$ from [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf], using [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. Steps 3--5 give
$$\Delta u=(1_A\otimes u)\Delta.$$
Define $h^\sharp=\epsilon u:A\to K$. Both factors are algebra maps (step 6 and the Hopf node), so [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives a point $h:\operatorname{Spec}K\to G$ over $K$, namely $h\in G(K)$.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, equivariance of comultiplication; Lemma 9.1, printed p.164.

proof.text:
Apply $1_A\otimes\epsilon$ to the equation of step 7. The counit identities of [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] give
$$u=(1_A\otimes h^\sharp)\Delta=r_A(h).$$
The last equality is exactly the evaluation formula of [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. Thus the point just constructed acts on the regular representation by $u$. This is the coordinate computation of Milne's Lemma 9.1, with $h^\sharp=\epsilon u$.

source.place: Lemma 9.1, printed p.164, evaluation at the identity.

proof.text:
For a finite-dimensional representation $V$ with coaction $c_V$, let $V_0$ be its underlying vector space with trivial action. The map $c_V:V\to V_0\otimes A$ is equivariant, since the required identity is precisely $(c_V\otimes1)c_V=(1\otimes\Delta)c_V$. It is injective because $(1_V\otimes\epsilon)c_V=1_V$. Both identities are supplied by [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary]. Apply enlarged naturality (step 3), tensor compatibility (step 4) and triviality (step 5) to obtain
$$c_V\lambda_V=(1_{V_0}\otimes u)c_V.$$
Equivariance of $c_V$ evaluated at $h$ also gives $c_V r_V(h)=(1_{V_0}\otimes r_A(h))c_V$. Step 8 identifies the right sides. Injectivity of $c_V$ gives $r_V(h)=\lambda_V$.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, embedding into the trivial space tensored with the regular representation; Proposition 4.12, printed pp.87--88.

proof.text: If $g\in G(K)$ also realizes the family, then $r_A(g)=u$: every $a\in A$ lies in a finite-dimensional rational submodule by [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subrepresentation], its inclusion into $A$ is equivariant by [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], and on that submodule both maps are $\lambda$. Applying $\epsilon$ to $r_A(g)=(1_A\otimes g^\sharp)\Delta$ gives $g^\sharp=\epsilon u=h^\sharp$, by the counit identity [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. The uniqueness of the affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $g=h$. This proves uniqueness without any reducedness or density assertion about $G(K)$.

source.place: Theorem 9.2, printed p.165, uniqueness; Lemma 9.1 and the counit identity.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 9.2, printed pp.164--165; Lemma 9.1, printed p.164; Remark 4.1 and Proposition 4.12.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-9a4b94033 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Milne iAG2017 Ch.9(a) pp.163-165 (regular representation (47), Lemma 9.1, conditions a-c, Thm 9.2), Ch.4(a) pp.83-84 (GL_V, comodule axioms (24), Remark 4.1 with (25)) and Prop 4.12. The item statement and stmt_deps are unchanged against live and side-live, where the item is still unsplit, and there is no repair note. The item is Thm 9.2 with R=K; its extra hypotheses (algebraically closed, finite type, invertible) are harmless and unused, and the statement is not weakened. Steps 1-10 follow Milne's proof: (2) extension via the finite-subcomodule node; (3) naturality, with Z⊗A→N⊗A injectivity written out via a basis of A; (4) tensor compatibility; (5) L_T=1 on trivial T, filling Milne's 'by (b)'; (6) m and unit equivariant, so u is an algebra map; (7) Δu=(1⊗u)Δ from coassociativity, h♯=εu; (8) u=(1⊗h♯)Δ=r_A(h), which is Lemma 9.1 in coordinates; (9) c_V:V→V0⊗A is an equivariant injection, so r_V(h)=λ_V; (10) uniqueness via ε∘r_A(g)=g♯ and the affine-spectrum bijection, with no faithful-representation or density claim, so it holds for nonreduced G. I checked the convention r(x)r(y)=r(xy) from (c⊗1)c=(1⊗Δ)c, and that c=Δ gives Milne's right regular representation. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. The new dictionary node is true and correctly hypothesised: it is Milne Remark 4.1 for V of any dimension, plus the morphism, trivial and tensor clauses and the finite-dimensional GL(V) clause. I tested V=0, trivial G, G_m, alpha_p and the regular comodule. It is unsplit and statement-only, with full stmt_deps and real searches, and it restates no clause of the item. A whole-DAG grep for comodule/coaction and natural-in-R/Aut_R found no duplicate (hopf-coaction-linearization, char-zero-differentiation-hom, comodule-finite-subrepresentation and coordinate-hopf all differ). There is no SGA source. review_split 'no such node' errors come from the symlinked chapter directories; I opened every one of those nodes. No fixes.
